clue.text: Nag CAMRA to move into stronger drink than ale

indicators.note: letters made to move around are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone urges the real-ale campaigners to switch to something stronger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to move' rearranges NAG and CAMRA. CAMRA is the Campaign for Real Ale, a British beer-drinkers' group, which makes the surface apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Armagnac is a French brandy, a spirit far stronger in alcohol than any beer.

clue.text: Impressionist portraying us in red and gold

indicators.note: in tells us one word sits inside the other

parts.note: rose is a shade of red
AU is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A painter depicts us in shades of red and gold.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a painter at work, but the 'Impressionist' is the definition and 'red and gold' supply the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Henri Rousseau was a French painter of the Post-Impressionist era, loosely an Impressionist.

clue.text: One's looking for workers in an American playhouse —— not hard

indicators.note: not hard tells us the letter for hard is to be removed

parts.note: theater is the American spelling of theatre
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A man is searching for staff for an American theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'workers' reads as staff, but here it means worker ants. American spelling of the playhouse is needed for the letters to fit.
explanation.definitionFit: An anteater feeds on ants and termites, so it is always looking for worker ants.

clue.text: Bromine only contains one element

indicators.note: contains signals that the answer is held within these two words

explanation.surface: Bromine is said to be made up of a single element.
explanation.definitionFit: Neon is a chemical element, one of the noble gases.

clue.text: Can't one ace go over a second in this game?

indicators.note: go over means to cover or surround, so one piece wraps around another

parts.note: the word as written, without its apostrophe
a single ace is an A in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A card player asks whether an ace may be played on top of another card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'go over' puts CANT around A S; the single ace, A, goes at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Canasta is a rummy-style card game in which aces have a part to play.

clue.text: Motorway intersection on the next page has caught learner previously

indicators.note: previously puts the caught and learner letters before the rest

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
L is for learner, as on British L-plates
overleaf means on the other side of the page

explanation.surface: A road junction is shown on the following page, which a learner driver read first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'previously' sets C and L before OVERLEAF.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloverleaf is a highway interchange whose looping slip roads look like a four-leaf clover.

clue.text: Sweet air must flow over one

indicators.note: over here means covering, so the shuffled letters go around the next piece
letters that flow move freely, so these two words are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Sweet air should pass over someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet' looks like an adjective describing the air, but it is the definition: a dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiramisu is an Italian dessert of coffee-soaked sponge and mascarpone, a sweet in British usage.

clue.text: Even though wounded, run for cover

indicators.note: wounded means damaged, so the letters of the word are disordered

parts.note: to lope is to run with long easy strides

explanation.surface: Though hurt, a soldier dashes for shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wounded' rearranges EVEN into ENVE.
explanation.definitionFit: An envelope is a paper cover for a letter; in general a covering or wrapper.

clue.text: Every American island's brief reference

parts.note: every, as in all of them

indicators.note: brief means cut short, so the last letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: Iona is a small island in the Scottish Hebrides; the 's links it to what follows

explanation.surface: An American island is mentioned only in passing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' cuts the last letter off IONA, leaving ION.
explanation.definitionFit: An allusion is an indirect reference to something, a passing mention.

clue.text: Pursue to the bitter end then wound savagely as energy fails

indicators.note: something done savagely is mangled, so these letters are thrown into a new order
when energy fails it drops out, so its letter is removed from the pool

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A hunter chases prey to the end and then wounds it brutally once tired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fails' takes E out of THEN WOUND, leaving THNWOUND, which 'savagely' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: To hunt down a quarry is to chase it relentlessly until it is caught.

clue.text: Support taking drink with added Ecstasy? That's not an answer

indicators.note: 'That's not an answer' tells us one A is to be taken away

parts.note: advocaat is a Dutch liqueur made with eggs and brandy
E is the street abbreviation for the drug Ecstasy

explanation.surface: Someone backs a drink spiked with Ecstasy and is told that is no solution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with added' puts E after ADVOCAAT; 'not' then removes one of its A's.
explanation.definitionFit: To advocate a cause is to support it publicly; both work as verbs.

clue.text: Write dull words when tossing off manuscript verse

parts.note: to pen is to write
tame means dull or unexciting

indicators.note: tossing off means throwing away, so these letters leave the word

parts.note: terms are words or expressions

explanation.surface: A writer produces boring prose while dashing off a manuscript.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tossing off' removes MS from TERMS, leaving TER.
explanation.definitionFit: Pentameter is a line of verse with five metrical feet, as in Shakespeare's blank verse.

clue.text: Confusing language, as Mark and Jack have different bosses

parts.note: an umbo is the central boss on a shield; each name has one
J is the card abbreviation for jack
a second umbo, the boss on a shield

explanation.surface: Two employees each answering to their own manager makes for baffling talk.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'bosses' are not managers but shield bosses: each of M and J gets its own UMBO.
explanation.definitionFit: Mumbo-jumbo is meaningless or deliberately obscure talk, gibberish.

clue.text: Prevail in fight with old drunk

parts.note: to prevail in a fight is to win it

explanation.surface: A drunk wins a brawl against an old opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: A wino is a habitual drinker, usually of cheap wine, so a drunk.

clue.text: Drink to engineers as the greatest

parts.note: to sup is to drink in sips
REME is the Royal Electrical and Mechanical Engineers, a British Army corps

explanation.surface: A toast is raised to engineers as the best.
explanation.walkthrough: REME, a British Army engineering corps, is a crossword regular for engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: Supreme means highest in rank or quality, so the greatest of all.

clue.text: What sailor may have longings to be accepted by group?

indicators.note: being accepted by a group means being taken inside it

parts.note: a set is a group
aches are longings or yearnings

explanation.surface: A homesick sailor hopes his yearnings will be understood by his crew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'longings' points to emotions, but it simply supplies aches, placed inside the group.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea chest is the box in which a sailor keeps personal belongings on board.

clue.text: Play with power and unusual energy opening in theatre

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power

indicators.note: unusual signals the letters are put into an odd order
the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A powerful, offbeat production opens in a theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusual' rearranges ENERGY into EERGYN; 'opening in' gives T.
explanation.definitionFit: Peer Gynt is a verse play by Henrik Ibsen.

clue.text: Sea god put erroneously in river

indicators.note: in places the shuffled letters inside the river's name

parts.note: the Nene is a river in eastern England

indicators.note: put erroneously means put wrongly, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A sea god has been mistakenly placed in a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Nene, a river in eastern England, is a crossword favourite because its letters are so handy.
explanation.definitionFit: Neptune is the Roman god of the sea, counterpart of the Greek Poseidon.

clue.text: Garment pockets

definitions.meaning: a pair of ... is an item of clothing
pockets as a verb, meaning takes money for oneself, often dishonestly

explanation.definitionFit: Trousers is a garment, and to trouser is slang for to pocket, as in trousers a fee.

clue.text: I take a dim view reporting what someone once did to the Portland vase?

indicators.note: reporting signals a phrase is spoken, giving its sound rather than its spelling

parts.words: what someone once did to the Portland vase
parts.note: in 1845 a visitor to the British Museum smashed the Portland vase, a Roman glass vessel: he knocked the urn over

explanation.surface: A sceptic recalls the vandal who smashed a famous vase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked urn' said quickly gives NOCTURNE. The 'I' speaks as a painting: a dim view is a night scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A nocturne is a painting of a night scene, so it gives a dark view.

clue.text: What Terminator did was better than following saint

indicators.note: following places the second piece after the first

parts.note: topped means outdid or bettered

explanation.surface: A film robot outdid a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'following' puts TOPPED after S.
explanation.definitionFit: A terminator brings things to an end, so what it did was halt them.

clue.text: Top copy's variable

parts.note: to ape is to copy or mimic
X is the usual algebraic symbol for an unknown variable

explanation.surface: A best copy is said to be variable.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is' and links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The apex is the highest point or tip of something, its very top.

clue.text: Openly gay, frequently a lot of our church is old-fashioned

parts.note: someone openly gay is out
oft is an old word for often, frequently

indicators.note: a lot of means most of the word, so its final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Being openly gay is often seen by much of our church as dated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot of' takes most of OUR, giving OU.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone out of touch has lost contact with current ideas, so is behind the times.

clue.text: Tough punishment suspending a paratrooper for ages?

definitions.meaning: a British idiom for being in for severe punishment
a playful reading: a jump from such height that the parachutist hangs in the air for a long time

explanation.surface: A paratrooper is punished by being left dangling for hours.
explanation.definitionFit: The high jump is both an athletic event and, in British idiom, a severe telling-off or punishment.

clue.text: Work regularly exhibited by rising sculptor

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters read upwards, backwards
regularly takes every other letter of the word

explanation.surface: A sculptor's work is shown at regular intervals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly exhibited by' takes SUPO from SCULPTOR; 'rising' turns it around.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a musical or artistic work, often numbered.

clue.text: What may amuse children, taking favourite tracks with young dog?

parts.note: a pup is a young dog
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet
RY is the abbreviation for railway, a set of tracks

explanation.surface: Children's entertainment involves a favourite puppy and train tracks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' and 'with' only join the pieces, which run PUP, PET, RY.
explanation.definitionFit: Puppetry, the art of puppet shows such as Punch and Judy, is a traditional children's entertainment.

clue.text: Senior prophetess reported to be prudent

parts.note: SEN is an abbreviation for senior

indicators.note: reported signals that the next word is spoken, giving a sound rather than a spelling

parts.note: a sibyl was a prophetess of the ancient world

explanation.surface: An elderly seer is said to be wise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reported' gives the sound of SIBYL, spelt SIBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sensible means showing good judgement, much as prudent means careful and wise.

clue.text: Catastrophe as star dies, shot

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or ruined, so these letters are broken up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A celebrity's death is a catastrophe, like a star shot down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a link; 'shot' rearranges STAR DIES.
explanation.definitionFit: A disaster is a sudden calamity causing great damage, a catastrophe.
